models.label: ECMWF IFS 0.25°
models.note: ECMWF's operational physics model, open-data release. Its gust field is a maximum over the output interval, not an instantaneous value, so gust factors look large in light air.

models.label: ECMWF AIFS
models.note: ECMWF's machine-learning model - a genuinely independent opinion. Publishes no gust field, so gusts come from IFS and ICON-2i only.

models.label: ItaliaMeteo ICON-2i
models.note: ItaliaMeteo / ARPAE high-resolution model for Italy - the finest grid available here. Runs only ~60-72 h ahead and updates every 12 h, so it drops out of the longer-range view.

models.label: Météo-France MFWAM
models.note: Full sea-state decomposition - total wave, wind wave and swell with heights, directions and periods.

models.label: ECMWF WAM 0.25°
models.note: Total significant wave height only - used to cross-check MFWAM.

briefing.headline: Very light, benign pattern over the Aeolians right now - but departure is 5 days out and only the first leg is in range.
briefing.synopsis: No forecast pressure fields are given in the payload, so I won't characterise the synoptic setup beyond what the wind data shows: a slack, low-gradient regime across all six islands, with consensus winds running 1-7 kt and a diurnal swing between a N/NE component by day and a S/SE component overnight at Portorosa (consensus values, sampled 6-hourly through 30 Sep). Seas are collapsing - wave and swell heights fall from about 0.9-1.2 ft on 28 Sep to 0.1 ft island-wide by 29-30 Sep. The model horizon here reaches only 04 Oct 23:00, so nothing beyond the first trip day is covered; anything I say about the trip week itself is pattern, not forecast.
briefing.overnight_anchorage: For the night of 03 Oct the fleet is scheduled at Portorosa Marina, and that is the recommendation - an enclosed marina with all-round shelter, so the choice does not matter. The forecast for that night is 3.9 kt SE, gusting 8.7 kt, with 0.1 ft swell from the NNE. Nothing in the payload would push the fleet elsewhere; a marina berth is indifferent to direction in any case.
briefing.tomorrow_morning: Tomorrow is not a trip day - the fleet is still five days from departure. For the first trip morning, 04 Oct, the ECMWF-based leg data shows a 06:00 start in 6.0 kt SE, gusting 11.5 kt, 0.1 ft sea, a run at 160 TWA; the window stays workable through a 14:00 departure with wind easing to 5.0 kt and veering NE by early afternoon. No deterioration time is flagged in that window, but expect this to be rewritten several times before the day arrives.

passage_notes.note: Only leg in range. Verdict 'go', best start 06:00, 5-6 kt SE easing and backing to NE by midday, 0.1 ft sea - likely a motor or motorsail for much of it. Overnight at Lipari: Porto Pignataro recommended (4.4 kt NE, 0.1 ft NNW swell); Marina Lunga and Valle Muria both score as sheltered too.
Beyond the model horizon (04 Oct 23:00). No forecast.
Beyond the horizon. Note that Marina del Gabbiano at Stromboli scores only 'workable' in the rehearsal - open from every direction, shelter depends on it staying calm.

passage_notes.leg: Rehearsal run (legs sailed against live 29 Sep - 04 Oct weather)
passage_notes.note: Every leg scored 'go' on 4 kt or less; several are head-to-wind motoring. This is a dry run of the routing logic, not a forecast for the trip dates.

cautions: Trip dates 05-08 Oct are outside every model's range in this payload. Treat the rehearsal 'go' verdicts as a test of the analysis, not as weather for the trip.
Model spread at Portorosa is wide in the light air - 1.2 to 9.6 kt at 00Z 28 Sep and 0.7 to 7.6 kt at 12Z - so a stated mean of 4-5 kt could be near-calm or a sailable breeze.
Gust figures from ECMWF IFS (28 Sep 06Z) are interval maxima, not instantaneous: 10-15 kt gusts against 2-5 kt means across the islands are an artefact of light air, not squalls.
Stromboli's Marina del Gabbiano is open from all directions; if the pattern is not this calm on the night, the optional Stromboli leg is the first thing to drop.
briefing.confidence_note: Wind-speed run-to-run stability is good (mean shift 0.8 kt at 72-120 h across 23 snapshots), but direction scatters by a mean 67 degrees at that lead and five of six legs sit past the 04 Oct 23:00 horizon entirely.

verification.measures: forecast stability, not verified accuracy - the reference is the newest model run for the same hour, not an observation
